claim_1.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from YF17D-vaccinated individuals in the Montreal cohort on day 0 and days 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60 after vaccination, using LIMMA differential expression analysis, showed that 594 genes changed significantly in at least one comparison versus day 0.

sources.quote: RNA samples obtained from whole blood of 15 YF17D-vaccinated individuals (from the Montreal cohort) on the day of vaccination (day 0) and at several time points after vaccination (day 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60) were amplified and hybridized onto Illumina chips and analyzed. Expression profiles of 594 genes (Supplemental document 1, available at http://www.jem.org/cgi/content/full/jem.20082292/DC1) were found to change significantly between day 0 and any time point after vaccination (with P < 0.05 and fold change less than −1.3 or >1.3).

Figure 1. Vaccination with YF17D induces early gene modulation. Global view of gene modulation in total blood cells after YF17D vaccination, as analyzed by gene array on the Montreal cohort (n = 9–15, depending on the time point). Heat map representation (a) and PCA (b) using the significantly modulated genes, in at least one comparison versus day 0.

claim_2.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from YF17D-vaccinated individuals in the Montreal cohort on day 0 and days 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60 after vaccination, using heat map representation and principal component analysis, showed that gene expression modulation was greatest at days 3 and 7 among the measured post-vaccination timepoints.

sources.quote: The peak of modulation of gene expression, as shown by heat map representation (Fig. 1 a) and principal component analysis (Fig. 1 b), primarily occurred at days 3 and 7 after vaccination, whereas a limited number of significant genes were modulated in response to vaccination at day 10 after vaccination or beyond.

Figure 1. Vaccination with YF17D induces early gene modulation. Global view of gene modulation in total blood cells after YF17D vaccination, as analyzed by gene array on the Montreal cohort (n = 9–15, depending on the time point). Heat map representation (a) and PCA (b) using the significantly modulated genes, in at least one comparison versus day 0.

claim_6.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from the Montreal cohort of 20 volunteers after a single YF17D vaccination, using LIMMA differential-expression analysis, showed that 43 genes encoding ribosomal proteins were down-regulated early after vaccination compared to day 0.

sources.quote: Strikingly, we observed that 43 genes encoding ribosomal proteins were down-regulated in PBMCs early after vaccination with YF17D (Supplemental document 1), confirming the findings of a previous study (15).

claim_7.claim: qPCR analysis of RNA from independent YF17D vaccination trials in the Montreal cohort, Lausanne cohort (13 volunteers), and Emory cohort (10 volunteers), at day 0 and day 7 after vaccination, showed that most genes up-regulated in the Montreal cohort also had increased fold-change expression in the Lausanne and Emory cohorts compared to baseline.

sources.quote: The results illustrated in Fig. 4 and in Fig. S3 indicate that most genes that were up-regulated in the Montreal cohort also showed increased expression in the two other independent trials.
Figure 4. Heat map of fold change gene expression between day 0 and 7, as measured by qPCR. For a complete heat map of all measured fold changes see Fig. S3.

claim_8.claim: qPCR analysis of RNA from independent YF17D vaccination trials in the Montreal cohort, Lausanne cohort (13 volunteers), and Emory cohort (10 volunteers), at day 0 and day 7 after vaccination, showed that most genes down-regulated in the Montreal cohort also had decreased fold-change expression in the Lausanne and Emory cohorts compared to baseline.

sources.quote: Conversely, most down-regulated genes in the Montreal cohort also showed decreased levels of expression in the samples obtained from the two other trials.
Figure 4. Heat map of fold change gene expression between day 0 and 7, as measured by qPCR. For a complete heat map of all measured fold changes see Fig. S3.

claim_9.claim: Microarray analysis of whole-blood RNA from the Montreal cohort (20 volunteers) at day 3 after YF17D vaccination, using LIMMA differential expression analysis and heat-map display of up-regulation, showed that CASP1 and CASP5 mRNA were up-regulated compared to day 0 baseline.

sources.quote: Our gene array results showed that two components of the inflammasome, caspase-1 and -5, were up-regulated at the mRNA level in the Montreal cohort, 3 d after vaccination with YF17D (Fig. 5 a).

Figure 5. YF17D induces expression of genes associated with IL-1β and activates the inflammasome. (a) Heat maps showing the up-regulation of genes encoding inflammasome components and the modulation of other, IL-1β–associated genes.

claim_10.claim: Microarray analysis of whole-blood RNA from the Montreal cohort (20 volunteers) at an unspecified post-vaccination timepoint after YF17D vaccination, using LIMMA differential expression analysis, probe-level consideration restricted to probes targeting all transcripts for IL-1R2 and IL-1RN, and heat-map display of modulation, showed that IL-1R2 and IL-1RN mRNA were modulated compared to day 0 baseline.

sources.quote: Two other genes related to IL-1β production and signaling that were modulated by the vaccine are IL-1R2 and -1RN.

(a) Heat maps showing the up-regulation of genes encoding inflammasome components and the modulation of other, IL-1β–associated genes. For IL-1R2 and -1RN only probes targeting all transcripts were considered.

claim_11.claim: Microarray analysis of whole-blood RNA from the Lausanne cohort (13 volunteers) at an unspecified post-vaccination timepoint after YF17D vaccination, using LIMMA differential expression analysis, probe-level consideration restricted to probes targeting all transcripts for IL-1R2 and IL-1RN, and heat-map display of modulation, showed that CASP1, IL-1R2, and IL-1RN mRNA were similarly modulated compared to day 0 baseline.

sources.quote: All of these genes, except for caspase-5, were also similarly modulated in the Lausanne cohort.

(a) Heat maps showing the up-regulation of genes encoding inflammasome components and the modulation of other, IL-1β–associated genes. For IL-1R2 and -1RN only probes targeting all transcripts were considered.

claim_21.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of DC/T cell co-cultures from YF-naive individuals after 14 d co-culture, using short restimulation with autologous DC targets left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D, showed that live or UV-inactivated YF17D-pulsed DCs primed a strong antigen-specific response with CD154 and IFN-γ expression in live CD4+-gated events compared to untouched autologous DC targets.

sources.quote: As shown in Fig. 8 a, DCs pulsed with YF17D virus (live or UV-inactivated) primed a strong antigen-specific response of naive T cells, with up to 4% cells expressing CD154 and IFN-γ in response to live or UV-inactivated YF17D.

(a and b) Purified T helper cells were mixed with DCs that had been incubated with live or UV-inactivated YF17D. After 14 d, the cells were harvested and evaluated by flow cytometry for cytokine and CD154 expression after a short restimulation with autologous DCs targets that had been left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D. All data plots show live CD4+-gated events. These are representative data of experiments done on cells from at least 10 volunteers.

claim_22.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of DC/T cell co-cultures from YF-naive individuals after 14 d co-culture, using short restimulation with autologous DC targets left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D, showed that YF17D-pulsed DCs stimulated antigen-specific Th2 cells expressing IL-5 and IL-13 in live CD4+-gated events compared to untouched autologous DC targets.

sources.quote: Similarly, YF17D-pulsed DCs stimulated high numbers of antigen-specific Th2 cells expressing IL-5 and IL-13, upon restimulation with live or inactivated virus (Fig. 8 b).

(a and b) Purified T helper cells were mixed with DCs that had been incubated with live or UV-inactivated YF17D. After 14 d, the cells were harvested and evaluated by flow cytometry for cytokine and CD154 expression after a short restimulation with autologous DCs targets that had been left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D. All data plots show live CD4+-gated events. These are representative data of experiments done on cells from at least 10 volunteers.

claim_23.claim: Multiplex cytokine analysis of culture supernatants from YF-naive individuals after 14 d DC/T cell co-culture showed that IL-2, IFN-γ, IL-13, and IL-5 levels were high when YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen compared to co-cultures with no recall antigen.

sources.quote: When YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen, the cells produced high levels of all the cytokines measured except IL-10, compared with co-cultures with no recall antigen.
(c) Alternatively, the culture supernatants were harvested and evaluated by a multiplex cytokine analysis. Data representative of experiments done on cells from two volunteers.

claim_24.claim: Multiplex cytokine analysis of culture supernatants from YF-naive individuals after 14 d DC/T cell co-culture showed that IL-10 was not produced at high levels when YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen compared to co-cultures with no recall antigen.

sources.quote: When YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen, the cells produced high levels of all the cytokines measured except IL-10, compared with co-cultures with no recall antigen.
(c) Alternatively, the culture supernatants were harvested and evaluated by a multiplex cytokine analysis. Data representative of experiments done on cells from two volunteers.
